newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech finmin backs cenbank markets watchdog plan.
newsitem.headline: Czech finmin backs cenbank markets watchdog plan.

text.p: Czech Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said on Thursday that he agrees with a central bank plan to coordinate supervision of the banks, capital markets, funds, and insurance market under one umbrella organisation.
But he added that new market regulations should not go so far as to choke free-market principles.
"One thought in that (Czech National Bank) proposal is precious, and that is coordination of the supervision," Kocarnik told reporters.

"Information on one subject on the capital market etc., or on the money market, in relation to another subject can be relevant to the supervisory functions. From this point of view the coordination is necessary."

Last week the CNB submitted a report to parliament analysing the economy in light of the failure of Plzen-based Kreditni Banka a.s. in August and its implications within the capital markets and investment funds.

The CNB said Kreditni's connection to the secretive investment group Motoinvest -- which also had investment connections to the largest private bank Agrobanka a.s. -- caused a crisis in confidence in Agrobanka.
Agrobanka saw its liquidity dry up, and the central bank put it under forced administration in September.
The CNB in its report blamed lax supervision of the markets, which falls under the finance ministry, for the problems of transparency and faith in the capital markets.

Kocarnik said it was first necessary to solve a number of other questions before such a wide-reaching body could be created, such as laws on banking secrecy and redefining the individual roles of capital market supervision.
The minister said he agreed that capital market supervision should be taken out of the finance ministry.

"But we have to clarify what will be the subject of the regulation...if it will be observance of law in the liberal understanding or if it will be an attempt to push for some far stricter rules, which are not necessarily effective."

He said he did not yet have enough information to comment on efforts by Prague Stock Exchange chairman and Civic Democratic Party colleague Tomas Jezek to set up an American-style independent Securities and Exchange Commission.
Jezek has gathered market experts to explore creating an SEC funded by a fee on each securities transaction.
